standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient topology on the target of a surjective map, and the notions of the strongest topology making a map continuous
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on submersive maps, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the three descriptions whose equivalence the statement asserts.

core_obligations: The candidate topology: the proof defines the family of subsets whose preimage is open and checks the topology axioms, using that preimages preserve the empty set, the whole set, unions and intersections (proof lines 704-710).

Maximality: it observes that any topology making the map continuous must be contained in this family, so this is the strongest such topology, which gives the equivalence with the first description (proof lines 710-730).

The closed-set description: the identity expressing the preimage of a complement as the complement of the preimage converts the description by opens into the description by closed sets (proof lines 731-732).
Conclusion: the three descriptions define the same topology on the quotient (proof line 732).
proof_roadmap: 先验证 {V ⊂ Y : f^{-1}(V) 开} 是拓扑：原像保持空集、全集、并与交。
再由任何使 f 连续的拓扑都包含其中，得到它是最强拓扑；用补集原像的恒等式把开集描述翻成闭集描述。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the triple description of the quotient topology (author lemma at source lines 691-701, label lemma-quotient): it is the strongest topology making the surjection continuous, and its opens and closed sets are exactly those with open resp. closed preimages. The proof (source lines 703-733) is a complete verification: the family of subsets with open preimage is shown to be a topology (proof lines 704-710), maximality among topologies making the map continuous is checked (proof lines 710-730), and the closed-set form is obtained from the preimage-of-complement identity (proof lines 731-732). The lemma is the companion of the induced-topology lemma and is the reference point for the chapter's results on submersive maps. H2.
